menopauseCard.title: In Menopause
menopauseCard.intro: Your body is going through a different phase now — no pressure to track a cycle. Fatigue, hot flashes and energy swings are a normal part of this chapter, not a failure. Listen to what you need today.
menopauseCard.stagesTitle: Menopause stages — see where you recognize yourself
menopauseCard.stagesHint: Tap to mark the stage you're in right now — you can change it anytime. If you're not sure, feel free to leave it unselected.
menopauseCard.unselectedMessage: Fatigue, hot flashes and energy swings are a normal part of this chapter, not a failure. You'll find tips for you here.

perimenopauza_skora.name: Early perimenopause
perimenopauza_skora.message: The first sign is usually a change in cycle length — a week or more, sometimes a skipped cycle. Hot flashes, mood or sleep changes can show up now too, though not yet in full force.
symptoms: a more irregular cycle (shifting by 7+ days)
perimenopauza_skora.keywords: first signs • awareness • sensitivity • new beginning
perimenopauza_skora.mantra: I am starting to notice the change.

perimenopauza_neskora.name: Late perimenopause
perimenopauza_neskora.ageRange: usually a few years before your last period
perimenopauza_neskora.message: Cycles are now clearly irregular, with gaps of 60 days or more. Hot flashes, night sweats, sleep disturbances and mood swings tend to be at their most intense right now — hormones are fluctuating the most, just before your period stops for good.
symptoms: more intense hot flashes and night sweats
perimenopauza_neskora.mantra: I let go of what no longer serves me.

menopauza.name: Menopause
menopauza.message: Menopause isn't a period of time, but a single point in time — a day confirmed retrospectively, once you've gone 12 months without a period. Your ovaries have stopped releasing eggs and producing estrogen at previous levels. What you're feeling now is usually a continuation of what started in late perimenopause, not something entirely new.
symptoms: hot flashes and night sweats may still linger
sleep and mood disturbances are fading slowly

postmenopauza.name: Postmenopause
postmenopauza.ageRange: from confirmed menopause for the rest of your life
postmenopauza.message: Hot flashes and night sweats usually ease over time — on average about 4.5 years after your last period, although about a third of women still feel them 10 years later. Other changes deserve attention, not waiting: bone loss is accelerating the most right now, and cardiovascular risk catches up to men of the same age within a few years. Dryness, discomfort during sex, or frequent urges to urinate also won't resolve on their own — but they can be treated well, all it takes is talking to your doctor about it.
symptoms: hot flashes gradually ease (4-5 years on average, longer for some)
accelerated bone loss — watch your movement and calcium
dryness or discomfort that won't resolve on its own — treatable
postmenopauza.mantra: I am free to be myself.

soulNotes.1: New life is quietly growing within — trust what you can't see yet.
soulNotes.2: You feel the first movements and the connection deepens — body and soul are learning together to be two.
soulNotes.3: You're approaching the big meeting. Your body knows what to do — trust its wisdom.

pregnancy.tipsIntro: Body, mind and ritual go hand in hand in pregnancy — food, movement and what you pay attention to are all part of the same journey. Every one of us experiences it differently and in our own way, so take this as inspiration, not a strict prescription.
pregnancy.partnerNote: This time isn't just yours — it's your partner's journey too. Let them be there with you: at check-ups, packing the hospital bag, during perineal massage, in conversations about what you feel and what you're afraid of. It's not a test you have to pass alone — you're a new family learning this together, from day one.
pregnancy.lateNote: Raspberry leaf is linked in some studies to a shorter second stage of labor when drunk gradually from around week 32-34 (start with one cup a day, then add more) — the evidence is still modest, not certain, so always run it by your midwife or gynecologist first. Lemon balm is calming and helps with insomnia or restlessness, and is generally considered safe — but herbal teas in pregnancy are recommended to be kept to around 1-2 cups a day. We deliberately don't mention chamomile — in the third trimester its effect on the uterus is assessed inconsistently. Lady's mantle is often paired with these in folk tradition, but safety data for pregnancy is lacking — better to skip it unless your doctor specifically recommends it. Perineal massage, on the other hand, has solid evidence that from around week 34-35 it reduces the risk of injury during birth — only do it when you genuinely feel ready, with your partner if you like.

5.message: The cells have just settled into the uterus and are dividing into layers that will form all the organs. The neural tube — the foundation of the brain and spinal cord — is beginning to close, and the heart, still just a tiny tube, will beat for the first time by the end of this period.

7.message: The heart is now beating regularly. The basics of the limbs and face are forming. This period often brings the first visit to the gynecologist.

9.message: Around this time the embryo officially becomes a fetus. All the major organs — heart, brain, kidneys, liver — have already begun forming, and the arms and legs are growing.
symptoms: mild cramping as the uterus enlarges

11.message: Fingers and toes are separating and nails are starting to grow. Bones are beginning to harden, and the baby can already make a fist, although you can't feel it yet.
symptoms: nausea starts easing for many women
a bump may already be showing

13.message: The baby is learning to swallow and suck, vocal cords are forming, and the kidneys are producing urine. The risk of miscarriage drops significantly after this point, which brings relief to many women — and first-trimester screening is usually done now too.

16.message: The baby can make facial expressions, hair and eyebrows are growing, and it's moving more (you still can't feel it). Many women get their energy back now — it's called the second-trimester glow.

20.message: Around this time (often toward the end of it, with a first baby) you'll feel movement for the first time. The baby is developing a protective coating and weighs about half a kilo by week 20. The big anatomy ultrasound is also done now.
symptoms: a darker linea nigra on the belly

24.message: The brain is growing rapidly, and the lungs are starting to produce the substance needed for breathing, though it's not mature yet. Around this point the theoretical threshold of viability outside the womb is reached — distant, but from now on it's worth paying attention to how regularly your baby moves.

27.message: After months of being shut, the eyes are opening again, and the baby responds to light and sound. Weight is increasing quickly. The gestational diabetes test is usually due around now.

31.message: You're entering the third trimester. The baby now has regular sleep-wake cycles, the brain is forming visible folds, and it's practicing breathing. Check-ups are usually every two weeks now.
symptoms: shortness of breath (the uterus is pressing on the lungs)

35.message: The baby is gaining fat, bones are formed but still soft — the skull stays soft for birth. Most babies turn head-down around now. The Group B strep test is approaching.
symptoms: more noticeable back and pelvic pain (loosened ligaments)

38.message: The baby is approaching full term, losing its fine body hair, and getting its reflexes ready for birth. The head often settles deeper into the pelvis, which can ease breathing but adds pressure lower down.
symptoms: easier breathing, but more pelvic pressure
stronger, more frequent Braxton Hicks contractions

41.message: This last stretch before birth can be incredibly tough — you're tracking the days around your due date almost constantly, and the waiting itself is exhausting, maybe more than anything before it. If you've already passed your due date, it doesn't mean anything's wrong — it's just an estimate, and if your cycle wasn't regular before conceiving, your actual gestational age could be different from what the date shows. Check-ups are a bit more frequent now, but that's just care, not a reason to worry. Hang in there — meeting your baby really is close now.

fallback.message: You're at the very edge of what this app can show week by week — the baby has long been ready, organs are mature. Monitoring from your gynecologist continues even more closely now. Trust your body and the team around you — the end really is close.
symptoms: possible loss of the mucus plug
waves of energy alternating with fatigue

postpartumCard.title: Šestonedelie
postpartumCard.tipsTitle: Food, movement and rituals for šestonedelie
postpartumCard.hydrationNote: Don't forget to drink — especially while breastfeeding it's easy to forget, even though your body needs even more water now than before. If healing is taking longer than you expect, or something feels off with your pelvic floor, a pelvic floor physiotherapist can help much faster than you'd think.
postpartumCard.enterBirthDate: Enter your baby's birth date in your profile.

postpartum.partnerNote: Šestonedelie isn't a test you have to endure alone — it's also a time when your partner is learning to be a parent too. Let them take on what they can — housework, night wakings, visitors — so you can heal and get to know your baby. You're a new family, and this is shared work from day one, not something only one of you has to carry.

1.message: The first week is about survival and getting to know each other. Bleeding is now at its heaviest and dark red, uterine contractions (felt most during breastfeeding) are at their strongest — this is how the uterus returns to its size. Around days 3–5, many women get a wave of crying or heightened sensitivity — it's called the baby blues and usually resolves on its own within two weeks. You and your baby are, above all, a new family right now — you have the right to set your own boundaries from the very start: who to let visit and when, what you need right now, when you want it to be just the two of you. Nothing else takes priority over this relationship.
symptoms: tenderness of the perineum or C-section scar
1.keywords: survival • getting to know • fragility • new beginning
1.mantra: I am being born too, right now.

2.message: Bleeding is turning lighter, pinkish to brownish. Cramps and breast tenderness should gradually be easing. The baby blues should be fading by the end of this week — if sadness or anxiety are getting stronger instead, it's time to ask for help, not just push through.
2.mantra: I am learning to trust my body and myself.

3.message: Bleeding is now light, yellowish to white, and may only show up occasionally. This period is also the most common onset of postpartum depression — not because you're doing anything wrong, but because your body and hormones are going through a huge change. If sadness, anxiety or a feeling of disconnection from your baby last longer than a few days, don't close yourself off — reach out to someone you trust (a friend, DIVA CIRCLE) as well as your gynecologist or pediatrician. Help works, and you don't have to wait for the six-week check-up, or handle it alone.
symptoms: a more sensitive mood — pay attention to how you feel
3.keywords: darkness • support • truth • you're not alone
3.mantra: I am not alone, even when it feels that way.

4.message: The uterus is nearing its original size, and the scar — whether from birth or a C-section — should feel noticeably calmer. Around this time, some women start losing more hair. It's a normal reaction of the body to the hormone drop, not something you did wrong.
4.mantra: My body remembers how to heal.

6.message: Bleeding should be stopping around now. Your six-week gynecologist check-up is approaching — a good opportunity to talk through everything you're feeling, physically and emotionally. Your pelvic floor muscles are still noticeably weaker than before pregnancy — exercises to strengthen them genuinely matter now, it's not just a formality.
symptoms: for C-section: usually cleared for normal activities
6.mantra: I am slowly coming home — to myself.

8.message: Most women are bleeding-free by now and cramps are gone. If you're not breastfeeding, your period may return; if you're exclusively breastfeeding, it may be delayed for months. Note — fertility can return even before your first period does. At your six-week check-up you may have gotten medical clearance for sex — but that's only permission, not an obligation. It's completely fine if you don't feel ready yet, whether that's now, in a month, or later. If you're breastfeeding, lower desire isn't just in your head — breastfeeding raises prolactin, which naturally suppresses libido. Nature set it up this way on purpose, so your body isn't banking on another pregnancy right now. Both body and mind take their own time with this, not the calendar's.
symptoms: possible return of your period (if not breastfeeding)

12.message: Physical healing is complete for most women by now. Hair loss may be at its peak — hang in there, it settles within a year. Core and pelvic floor strength are still gradually returning, especially if you keep working on them regularly.
symptoms: gradually returning core and pelvic floor strength
12.mantra: I am joining who I was with who I am now.

fallback.message: You've been on this new path for several months now. Hair settles within a year, the scar keeps maturing for months, and the pelvic floor and core keep strengthening with regular exercise. Healing, hormones and the bond with your child all move at their own pace — trust it, it's not a race.
symptoms: energy and libido return at their own individual pace
fallback.keywords: balance • wholeness • mother and woman • your own pace
fallback.mantra: I can be a mother and myself, both at once.

ttc.intro: You're trying to conceive — the days around ovulation are highlighted in color in the calendar below. Tap a day to privately log when you were intimate.
ttc.mantra: I trust my body and its own timing.
ttc.timelineNote: About 30% of women conceive in their very first cycle, 66–80% within 6 months, and around 85% within a year of trying regularly. If you've been trying for 9 months, you're still well within the normal range — it not having happened yet doesn't mean something's wrong.
ttc.stressNote: Important: there's no evidence that stress directly causes infertility. If this is hard, it's hard on its own terms — not because you haven't "relaxed enough." Taking care of yourself matters for you, not as a way to "pray it into happening."
ttc.emotionalNote: Sadness, anxiety and the two-week wait for a test result are real and valid — not an overreaction. Talking to someone who understands (a partner, friends, a support group, counseling) genuinely helps carry it.
ttc.ageUnder35: Under 35, a check-up is usually recommended after 12 months of trying regularly without conceiving.
ttc.age35Plus: From 35, it's after 6 months, and over 40 it's good to consult sooner rather than waiting.
soonerIf: a diagnosis of PCOS, endometriosis or fibroids
a known or suspected factor on your partner's side
ttc.mythsTitle: Myths you can let go of

myths.myth: After sex you need to lie with your legs up for a while.
myths.fact: It doesn't change anything — sperm reach where they need to within minutes, regardless of position.

myths.myth: A specific sex position is better for conceiving.
myths.fact: No research confirms that sex position affects the chance of conception.

myths.myth: If you didn't have an orgasm, your chances are lower.
myths.fact: You can conceive with or without an orgasm — it's not a requirement.

menstruacna.name: Menstrual phase
menstruacna.description: You're in your inner winter. The body goes quiet and asks for rest — like nature in January. It's not weakness, it's the body's wisdom: only do as much as you feel up to.

folikularna.name: Follicular phase
folikularna.description: You're entering your inner spring. Hormones are waking up, your head clears, and the urge to create grows with each day — a great time for new challenges, strength training and longer runs.

ovulacia.name: Ovulation
ovulacia.description: You're in your inner summer. The sun is at its highest — energy, confidence and the urge to be around people are all at their peak — time for personal records and community activities.

lutealna.name: Luteal phase
lutealna.description: You're entering your inner autumn. Energy slowly quiets down and your body invites you to harvest — finish what you started, and choose gentler movement: yoga, walks, recovery.

menstruacna_tazke_dni.name: Winter — the deepest dark
menstruacna_tazke_dni.description: The first days tend to be the hardest, just like the shortest days of the year. Energy is at its lowest, so let yourself stop — warmth, calm, and nothing to prove.

menstruacna_doznievanie.name: Winter — the light is returning
menstruacna_doznievanie.description: Bleeding is easing, strength is slowly coming back, as if the days were growing a little longer again. If you feel like moving, pick a short walk, but don't push yourself.

folikularna_rozbeh.name: Spring — the first buds
folikularna_rozbeh.description: Hormones are rising and your head clears, as if the first buds were sprouting from the ground. A great time to launch new ideas and plans.

folikularna_vrchol.name: Spring — full bloom
folikularna_vrchol.description: You're in great shape — energy, self-confidence and performance are growing as fast as spring greenery. Your body can handle more demanding training now.

ovulacia.name: Summer — full sun
ovulacia.description: You're at the peak of your cycle, just like the sun on the longest day of the year. Energy, confidence and the urge to be around people are all at their highest — time for personal records.

lutealna_stabilna.name: Autumn — harvest time
lutealna_stabilna.description: Energy is still good, just slowly settling, like warm September days. Finish what you've started while you still have the strength for it.

lutealna_premenliva.name: Autumn — the wind is changing
lutealna_premenliva.description: Moods can shift and you're more sensitive, much like autumn weather changing. Be patient with yourself and don't plan anything demanding for these days.

lutealna_neskora.name: Autumn — the last leaves fall
lutealna_neskora.description: Energy is at its lowest and PMS is at its strongest, right before calm winter arrives. Give yourself rest, gentleness and as few obligations as possible.

ovulacia.mantra: I am out in the world.

menstruacna.tagline: The cycle's inner winter — time to let go and go quiet.

folikularna.tagline: The cycle's inner spring — time to sprout and begin.

ovulacia.tagline: The cycle's inner summer — time to shine and connect.

lutealna.tagline: The cycle's inner autumn — time to harvest and slow down.
